{{Expand|TFF|FFD|BravelyD|FFCC|FFCC|FFCC|FFIV|FFIII|Info on formulas, character/job specifics, etc.}}
'''Speed''' {{J|すばやさ|Subayasa}}, also known as '''Dexterity''', '''Agility''', '''Agl''', or '''Mobility''', is a recurring [[Stats|statistic]] from the ''[[Final Fantasy series|Final Fantasy]]'' series. It determines how often a unit will attack. In games with time based battle systems, it is used to determine the rate at which the ATB or [[Charge Time|charge time]] gauge rises. It can be augmented or reduced by [[Time Magic]] spells [[Haste (ability)|Haste]] or [[Slow (ability)|Slow]].

== Appearances ==
=== ''[[Final Fantasy]]'' ===
Agility increases a character's accuracy and evasion by 2 for each agility point gained from [[level]]-ups. Each point of agility gained as a result of equipment or the [[Speed Plus (Final Fantasy)|Speed Plus]] item will only increase accuracy and evasion by 1. The higher a character's agility, the more likely they are to make the first move in a turn.

Having a couple of points of agility more than a monster does not guarantee a successful first move each turn; it only increases the chance.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy II]]'' ===
Agility factors into [[evasion]], and hence contributes to evading attacks more effectively and action order in battle. Agility has a random chance of increasing after each battle, based on the character's Evasion-% stat. Hence, avoiding heavy armor and equipping shields or weapons with high evasion values will boost Agility growth.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy III]]'' ===
Agility determines how fast a character gets to act in combat compared to everyone else, how many hits they do when physically attacking and the hit/miss chance for each hit.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy IV]]'' ===
[[Final Fantasy IV stats#Speed|Speed]] determines how fast a character gets their turn and casts magic; the speed is also affected by the character's weapon.
{{Section|Final Fantasy IV}}

==== ''[[Final Fantasy IV -Interlude-]]'' ====
Speed determines how fast a character gets their turn and casts magic; the speed is also affected by the character's weapon.

==== ''[[Final Fantasy IV: The After Years]]'' ====
Speed determines how fast the character's turn will come up.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy V]]'' ===
{{See|Final Fantasy V jobs#List of Jobs and their stats|t1=List of jobs and their stats|Final Fantasy V agility bug}}
Agility determines the characters' battle speed and factors in some weapon damage calculations. The [[Battle Speed]] setting in the [[config]] determines how many turns opponents get, but does not affect the player party. A character's stats are determined by which [[Final Fantasy V jobs|job]] they are using. [[Thief (Final Fantasy V)|Thief]] is the fastest job, and [[Berserker (Final Fantasy V job)|Berserker]] the slowest. Thief can learn a skill called Agility, which makes any job as fast as a Thief.

The Agility stat determines the speed at which a unit's [[Active Time Battle]] bar fills up (along with [[Final Fantasy V stats#Weight|Weight]] for characters). Additionally, it contributes to the effect of many ranged physical weapons (such as [[Final Fantasy V weapons#Bows|bows]]) and [[Throw (Final Fantasy V)|throwing]] attacks. Whether it affects the damage dealt by physical weapons depends on the weapon equipped. However, due to a seeming programming oversight, the effect of agility stat to weapon damage is often negligible.

To prevent speed ties for characters in the same job, every character has a different inherent boost to Agility. From slowest to fastest: [[Galuf Halm Baldesion|Galuf]] (+0), [[Bartz Klauser|Bartz]] (+1), [[Lenna Charlotte Tycoon|Lenna]] (+2), [[Faris Scherwiz|Faris]] (+3), and [[Krile Mayer Baldesion|Krile]] (+4).

The [[Sing (Final Fantasy V)#Swift Song|Swift Song]] from the [[Bard (Final Fantasy V)|Bard]]'s [[Sing (Final Fantasy V)|Sing]] skillset boosts the party's Speed while the Bard is singing.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy VI]]'' ===
[[Final Fantasy VI stats#Speed|Speed]] determines the characters' battle speed. The battle speed setting in the config determines how many turns opponents get, but does not affect the player party. Each character has a set of base stats that are static, unless boosted by [[Esper (Final Fantasy VI)|espers']] level up abilities. Only two espers boost Speed: [[Odin (Final Fantasy VI)|Odin]] and [[Cactuar (Final Fantasy VI summon)|Cactuar]]; in the ''Pixel Remaster'' as of Ver1.0.6, Odin's bonus was switched to Speed +2, giving Odin's old bonus of Speed +1 to [[Quetzalli (Final Fantasy VI)|Quetzalli]]. [[Locke (Final Fantasy VI party member)|Locke]] has the highest natural Speed, and [[Strago (Final Fantasy VI party member)|Strago]] the lowest.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy VII]]'' ===
[[Final Fantasy VII stats#Dexterity|Dexterity]] determines the speed of which the units' ATB Gauge fills up (in conjunction with the [[battle speed]] setting in the config), as well as affecting the character's physical evasion in conjunction with the Defense % given in the character's armor.

Dexterity can be increased with the [[Speed Source]] item and with the [[Speed Plus (Final Fantasy VII)|Speed Plus]] [[Independent Materia (Final Fantasy VII)|Independent Materia]]. The maximum additional Dex that can be gained through the Speed Plus Materia is +100% when stacked with multiple Materia. The accessory [[Choco Feather (Final Fantasy VII)|Choco Feather]] also gives +10 to Dexterity.

The exact amount of Dexterity gain via leveling up is randomized at each gained level, but the game is programmed in a manner the characters never stray too far from the intended average.

==== ''[[Dirge of Cerberus -Final Fantasy VII-]]'' ====
Speed determines the rate of fire.

====''[[Final Fantasy VII Remake]]''====
[[File:Speed from FFVII Remake icon.png|20px|Speed.]]
Speed is a characters' [[Final Fantasy VII Remake attributes|attribute]] that determines how fast their ATB gauge charges passively. It is boosted by fist weapon upgrades.

====''[[Final Fantasy VII Rebirth]]''====
{{section|Final Fantasy VII Rebirth}}

=== ''[[Final Fantasy VIII]]'' ===
The Speed stat affects the rate the characters' ATB gauges fill up. The characters base stats are low, but of the main six playable characters [[Irvine (Final Fantasy VIII party member)|Irvine]] is the fastest and [[Quistis (Final Fantasy VIII party member)|Quistis]] the slowest. The stat can be boosted with [[Spd Up (Final Fantasy VIII)|Spd Up]] items (which are rare) and with the [[Stat-enhancing ability|Speed Plus %]] abilities some [[Guardian Force]]s can learn. Characters can boost their speed by [[Junction system|junctioning]] spells into their [[Spd-J]]—[[Triple (Final Fantasy VIII)|Triple]] is an especially useful spell for that.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy IX]]'' ===
Speed stat determines how fast the ATB gauge fills, but due to the way the attacks work, it has almost no impact on the actual gameplay. Speed increases as the characters level up, and can also be boosted by wearing certain pieces of [[Final Fantasy IX armor|equipment]]. [[Zidane (Final Fantasy IX party member)|Zidane]] is the only character who can max out his speed stat to 50 without the use of cheats. In Zidane's case, Speed is an important factor for damage in his [[Thievery (Final Fantasy IX)|Thievery]] skill.

Formula for Speed:
:<math>SpdBase + [Level \times 1 / 10] + [SpdBonus / 32]</math><ref>[http://www.gamefaqs.com/ps/197338-final-fantasy-ix/faqs/20745 ''Final Fantasy IX'' Max Stats FAQ by KADFC]</ref>

The SpdBase values differ from character to character, but never change. The SpdBonus is the only way the player can affect the Speed growth, and every level up the bonus goes up by a rate that is worked out from the character's current stat increases. For example, if the character has equipment that gives 3 extra Speed, then SpdBonus will go up 3 every time they level up. (See [http://www.gamefaqs.com/ps/197338-final-fantasy-ix/faqs/20745 ''Final Fantasy IX'' Max Stats FAQ by KADFC for more info]).

Mechanics-wise, the Speed stat reduces the "size" of the ATB bar so it takes fewer "ticks" to fill. However, everyone else's ATB gauges continue to fill during ability animations except for the character performing the ability, and thus most of the time when a character takes their turn, everyone else's bar will completely fill during the animation. Party members' actions thus queue up and happen one after the other, and by the time they are done, the first character's bar has filled and they have joined the queue. This means that the most the Speed stat can affect the turn order, but will rarely result in a character getting more turns than a slower character.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy X]]'' ===
[[Final Fantasy X stats#Agility|Agility]] determines how often a character gets a turn. Agility is increased by activating agility nodes on the [[Sphere Grid]]. [[Rikku (Final Fantasy X party member)|Rikku]] has the best Agility on her path; [[Auron (Final Fantasy X party member)|Auron]] and [[Lulu (Final Fantasy X party member)|Lulu]] have the worst; but eventually, any character can traverse any path on the grid. Agility Spheres can be farmed from [[Fenrir (Final Fantasy X)|Fenrir]] in the [[Monster Arena]] to further boost Agility.

The benefit of raising Agility caps off before reaching 255. The first turn of a battle may, from a technical point of view, come slightly quicker with higher Agility, up as far as 250; this is negated in the event of a [[attack formations#Final Fantasy X|Preemptive Strike]] or use of a [[First Strike (Final Fantasy X)|First Strike]] weapon. Apart from this first turn, the effect of raising Agility caps off at 170. The first turn effect is virtually negligible, therefore many players choose to stop raising Agility once they reach 170. The Standard Sphere Grid in its default configuration already contains enough Agility nodes to reach 170.

[[Aeon (Final Fantasy X)|Aeons]] have their own stats separate from the characters'. They are mainly based on [[Yuna (Final Fantasy X party member)|Yuna]]'s stats, but also can be boosted manually and increase when the player fights more battles. [[Shiva (Final Fantasy X)|Shiva]] is the fastest aeon, and [[Ixion (Final Fantasy X)|Ixion]] the slowest.

==== ''[[Final Fantasy X-2]]'' ====
Agility is used for the traditional ATB system to determine the battle unit's cooldown and charging time of the ATB gauge. The character's stats depend on which [[dressphere]] she is wearing; [[Berserker (Final Fantasy X-2)|Berserker]] is the fastest job and [[Dark Knight (Final Fantasy X-2)|Dark Knight]] the slowest. Furthermore, some accessories provide an increase to the user's Agility stat, while the Adamantite deducts 30 points from its wearer's Agility stat. Likewise, [[Creature Creator|captured creatures]] each have their base Agility stat that is later modified by accessories and dresspheres. Notably, L-sized creatures (e.g. [[Shell Shocker]] and [[Flan Azabache]]) have significantly higher Agility than usual to compensate for the fact they always fight alone.

The color for the Agility gauge in the menu is light blue.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy XI]]'' ===
Dexterity is a stat compared with an enemy's agility to determine the likelihood that a character's blow will be a [[critical hit]], and also plays a significant role in determining the damage caused by [[Sneak Attack (ability)|Sneak Attack]] when used by a [[Thief (Final Fantasy XI)|Thief]]. It is associated with the element of [[Lightning (element)|Lightning]], and thus many lightning-based items add DEX to a character's stats.

Dexterity also has a direct impact on a character's [[accuracy]] stat. For every two points of DEX a character has, his/her accuracy is raised by one point. When using a Two-Handed Weapon, for every 4 points of DEX, the player's accuracy value is raised by 3 (.75 per one point of DEX).

=== ''[[Final Fantasy XII]]'' ===
[[Final Fantasy XII stats#Speed|Speed]] affects the charge time to perform actions in conjunction with the battle speed setting in the config and which [[Final Fantasy XII weapons|weapon]] the character is using (some weapons are faster than others). Speed stat also boosts the power of [[Final Fantasy XII weapons#Bows|bows]], [[Final Fantasy XII weapons#Ninja swords|ninja swords]], and [[Final Fantasy XII weapons#Daggers|daggers]], and determines the character's [[Counter (ability)#Final Fantasy XII|counterattack]] rate. Some equipment also boosts Speed, especially the accessory [[Cat-ear Hood (Final Fantasy XII)|Cat-ear Hood]] in the original PlayStation 2 version, and the [[Germinas Boots (Final Fantasy XII)|Germinas Boots]] in the ''Zodiac'' versions.

The Speed stat is less significant than in the other games in the series. The charge time difference is only noticeable if a character has very low speed and the difference decreases as speed increases. Even for the extremes, the highest possible Speed (99) only makes charging 21% faster compared to the lowest possible Speed (23).

The damage daggers, ninja swords, and bows deal depends on both Strength and Speed. During low levels this offers a distinctive edge, but on higher levels, the edge is decreasingly obvious. The [[Haste (Final Fantasy XII status)|Haste]] and [[Berserk (Final Fantasy XII status)|Berserk]] statuses also influence the character's battle speed much more than their Speed stat.

The characters gain Speed as they level up. There are no significant differences between characters. The following formula determines a character's Speed:<ref name=FF12>{{ref |id=FF12 |author=Maltzsan|date=January 30, 2007|title=Final Fantasy XII Game Mechanics FAQ|url=https://www.neoseeker.com/final-fantasy-xii/faqs/142830-mech.html|platform=Neoseeker|access-date=1st September 2020}}</ref>
:<math>\text{Base} + (\text{Level} \times \text{Modifier})/128 </math>
:Base = Base value. Different character has different values.
:Level = The character's current level.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy XIV]]'' ===
[[Final Fantasy XIV stats#Dexterity|Dexterity]] increases [[Final Fantasy XIV stats#Attack Power|attack power]] and is the primary attribute for the following disciplines: 

{{icon|ffxiv|discipline|rogue}} / {{icon|ffxiv|discipline|ninja}}<br>
{{icon|ffxiv|discipline|archer}} / {{icon|ffxiv|discipline|bard}}<br>
{{icon|ffxiv|discipline|machinist}}<br>
{{icon|ffxiv|discipline|dancer}}

[[Final Fantasy XIV stats#Skill Speed|Skill speed]] reduces the cast time and cooldown on weaponskills, and reduces the delay on auto-attacks. [[Final Fantasy XIV stats#Speed Speed|Spell speed]] reduce the cast time and cool down on spells. [[Final Fantasy XIV stats#Haste|Haste]] combines the effects of skill speed and spell speed at a much higher coefficient, but is exclusively a Eureka Effect or Save the Queen Area Effect, meaning it works only in {{icon|ffxiv|duty|eureka}} and {{icon|ffxiv|duty|save the queen}} duties respectively.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Tactics]]'' ===
{{Quote|A combination of the unit's inherent speed and any job, equipment, or ability bonuses. A higher number means the unit's turn will come more quickly.|Description}}
[[Final Fantasy Tactics stats#Speed|Speed]] determines how often a unit gets a turn. Every tick, each character's CT increases by their Speed (for example, a character with 10 Speed has their CT increase by 10, a character with 3 increases their CT by 3, etc.). When the CT reaches 100, that character gets a turn. Speed maxes out at 50, as it is useless to have a Speed greater than it since the character will get a turn in two ticks anyway.

==== ''[[Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: The Crystal Bearers]]'' ====
Focus, represented by the [[Water (element)|water element]], is one of [[Layle]]'s five stats, which, like the other four, can be increased by equipping accessories. Focus determines how quickly Layle can lock-on to a target.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Mystic Quest]]'' ===
The higher the number, the better chances the character will attack first.

=== ''[[The Final Fantasy Legend]]'' ===
Agility is shortened to Agl. The higher the number, the greater the character's agility will be. The screen only displays a maximum of 99 agility, however, they may have up to 255 agility.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Legend II]]'' ===
Agility is abbreviated to Agl and influences how often the character can hit the target. It also shows how well they will do with [[Long Range|ranged]] and martial art skill weapons. Some weapons use the Agl stat instead of the usual [[Strength|Str]] stat for its damage formula. This stat impacts damage dealt with light swords, the ability to [[Escape (command)|run from enemies]], dodging enemy attacks, and most importantly, determines the sequence of turns in battle.

Units with higher Agl will act before those with lower Agl. It can be raised by equipping light swords and various other items for battle. Agl caps at 99, but can be raised higher than that by equipping certain items and armor such as [[Hermes Sandals|Hermes]].

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Legend III]]'' ===
The higher the character's Agility, the easier it is for the player to run from battle. Agility also affects a character's initiative, ability to do damage by swords, and accuracy of attack.

=== ''[[Final Fantasy Explorers]]'' ===
Mobility determines how fast a character can move. It can be increased by [[Equipment Traits]] and [[Haste (ability)#Final Fantasy Explorers|Haste]], or reduced by [[Slow (ability)#Final Fantasy Explorers|Slow]] and [[Final Fantasy Explorers statuses#Paralysis|Paralysis]]. Each class has a different base Mobility.
